title: Turning autovacuum off on the hottest table during business hours

source.note: Adapted from Sentry's 2015 transaction ID wraparound outage write-up.

input.objective: Remove the IO spikes that push p99 write latency of the event ingestion database above 500 ms during business hours.
constraints: Ingestion must keep up with ~25k inserts/s at peak.
input.context: PostgreSQL 9.4, single primary, ~3 TB. The `events` table receives ~25k inserts/s and periodic bulk deletes of expired rows; it is ~1.8 TB. IO graphs show the spikes coincide with autovacuum workers processing `events` (often running for many hours). Other tables are small and vacuum quickly. Nightly traffic is ~20% of peak.
input.proposed_solution: Set `autovacuum_enabled = false` on `events` and run `VACUUM ANALYZE events` from a cron job every Sunday at 02:00, when traffic is lowest. Keep autovacuum on for all other tables. Since `events` is append-mostly, dead tuples accumulate slowly and a weekly vacuum is enough to control bloat; the bulk deletes already run off-peak. We will watch table bloat in Grafana.

ground_truth.material_issue: Vacuum is not only about bloat: it freezes tuples to prevent transaction ID wraparound. At this write rate, a weekly manual vacuum of a 1.8 TB table may not finish and anti-wraparound vacuum gets deferred; when the limit nears, PostgreSQL forces aggressive vacuum or stops accepting writes. Should tune autovacuum (cost limits, per-table thresholds, more workers), partition the table so old partitions can be dropped instead of deleted, and monitor age(datfrozenxid).
required_observations: Vacuum also prevents transaction ID wraparound (freezing), not just bloat
A weekly vacuum on a 1.8 TB table may not complete; wraparound leads to forced shutdown / read-only
Tune autovacuum throttling instead, and/or partition and drop old partitions; monitor XID age
